classification.difficultyReason: Connects an immediate harvest with the initial condition, then uses supplied factorisation and partial fractions to solve the IVP and identify extinction.

content.prompt:
Biologists model a fish population $y$ (in hundreds) using:
$$\frac{dy}{dt}=-2+\frac{1}{24}y(16-y)$$
where $t$ is years after the next harvest. The December count indicates 500 fish. Assume the next harvest removes 200 fish immediately after this count.

children.label: a
children.prompt: What is the significance of the $-2$ in the equation?

answer.short: Fish are harvested at a rate of 200 fish per year.
answer.worked: Since $y$ is measured in hundreds of fish and $t$ in years, the term $-2$ represents removal of 200 fish per year.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Show the DE can be rewritten as $\dfrac{dy}{dt}=-\dfrac{1}{24}(y-4)(y-12)$, and write down the initial condition assuming the harvest goes ahead.

answer.short: $\dfrac{dy}{dt}=-\dfrac{1}{24}(y-4)(y-12)$. Assuming the next harvest removes 200 fish immediately, $y(0)=3$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dt}&=-2+\frac{1}{24}y(16-y)\\\frac{dy}{dt}&=\frac{1}{24}\bigl(-48+y(16-y)\bigr)\\\frac{dy}{dt}&=-\frac{1}{24}(y^2-16y+48)\\\frac{dy}{dt}&=-\frac{1}{24}(y-4)(y-12).\end{aligned}$$
The supplied solution assumes an immediate harvest of 200 fish. Under this assumption, $y(0)=\dfrac{500-200}{100}=3$.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Hence solve the IVP in part b.

answer.worked:
Using the supplied solution's assumption $y(0)=3$:
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dt}{dy}&=-\frac{24}{(y-4)(y-12)}\\\frac{dt}{dy}&=-\left(\frac{3}{y-12}-\frac{3}{y-4}\right).\end{aligned}$$
Integrating gives
$$\begin{aligned}-t+D&=3\ln|y-12|-3\ln|y-4|\\3\ln\left|\frac{y-12}{y-4}\right|&=-t+D\\\ln\left|\frac{y-12}{y-4}\right|&=-\frac{t}{3}+D_1\\\frac{y-12}{y-4}&=Ae^{-t/3}.\end{aligned}$$
Apply $y(0)=3$:
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{3-12}{3-4}&=Ae^0\\A&=9.\end{aligned}$$
Therefore
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{y-12}{y-4}&=9e^{-t/3}\\y-12&=9e^{-t/3}(y-4)\\y(1-9e^{-t/3})&=12-36e^{-t/3}\\y&=\frac{12-36e^{-t/3}}{1-9e^{-t/3}}\\y&=\frac{12(1-3e^{-t/3})}{1-9e^{-t/3}}.\end{aligned}$$

children.label: e
children.prompt: According to this model, when will the fish die out? Give an exact answer and an approximation to the nearest tenth of a year.

answer.short: Assuming $y(0)=3$, $3\ln3\approx3.3$ years after the next harvest.
answer.worked:
Using the solution with $y(0)=3$, extinction occurs when $y=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}1-3e^{-t/3}&=0\\e^{-t/3}&=\frac13\\-\frac{t}{3}&=-\ln3\\t&=3\ln3\\t&\approx3.3\text{ years}.\end{aligned}$$
The denominator is $1-9\left(\frac13\right)=-2\ne0$, so this gives zero population. The fish die out about 3.3 years after the next harvest.
